summary: Generation 3 was rejected after post-claim validation because its recovery basis adds only elapsed-time replaceability and no new byte source, evidence revision, artifact, capability, or retry-enabling condition. G1 and G2 already establish SOURCE_DEBT: the only committed V11 payload is corrupt, repository/history/export/linked-repo/File-Library/web evidence did not reproduce the required 69,235-byte HTML, and authentic recovery now requires a new external preserved artifact. Repeating the same archaeology would fabricate progress rather than recover bytes. No payload bytes or authority pointers were changed.

Allocator recovery should gate repeat generations for evidence-bound BOUNDARY/SOURCE_DEBT work on a changed recovery basis rather than elapsed time alone.

spawn_candidates.title: Gate SOURCE_DEBT recovery on new evidence
spawn_candidates.reason: This G3 was created only because G2 became time-replaceable even though G2 explicitly required an external artifact; without a new basis the recovery route cannot make progress.
acceptance: BOUNDARY/SOURCE_DEBT returns can remain visible nonterminal attention without automatically becoming time-only recovery candidates.
A new generation becomes claimable only when a durable recovery basis changes materially, such as new artifact/evidence revision, newly available required capability, or explicit retry-safe trigger.
Ordinary silent-owner stale recovery remains unchanged.
Regression proves repeated allocator builds do not increment generations for unchanged SOURCE_DEBT and do re-enable routing when a new basis appears.
